title: installer: add `verify-bundle` command (offline bundle verification stub + unit tests)
author: Ethan Park
body:
## Context
Private on-prem installs for regulated/air-gapped customers will use an "offline bundle" (images + charts + binaries + metadata) transferred via removable media or an offline repo. Before we unpack/install anything, we need a deterministic offline verification step.

This PR adds a new installer CLI subcommand, `verify-bundle`, as the first building block. It wires in manifest loading + digest checks and provides a signature verification interface (stubbed for now) so we can land the command/UX and start integrating it into the install flow in follow-up PRs.

Related: Linear ENG-3914

## What changed
- Added `redwood-private-installer verify-bundle` command.
- Implemented bundle manifest parsing + basic validation (presence, schema version field, required top-level keys).
- Implemented SHA-256 digest verification for files referenced by the manifest (fail-closed).
- Added signature verification interface and CLI wiring:
  - `SignatureVerifier` interface lives in `internal/verify/signature`.
  - Default implementation is a stub returning a typed `ErrSignatureVerificationUnimplemented`.
  - CLI returns a non-zero exit code when signature verification is unimplemented (so we don’t accidentally treat this as "verified" in automation).
- Added structured error handling with stable exit codes:
  - `0` = verification succeeded
  - `2` = verification failed (digest mismatch / missing file / signature error)
  - `3` = usage error (bad args)
- Added unit tests around argument parsing, manifest loading failures, digest mismatch behavior, and signature stub behavior.

## Why a stub for signature verification?
Signing pipeline + signature envelope format are still in-flight. Landing the command now lets us:
- align on CLI UX and logging fields,
- start hooking verification into the installer flow early,
- build out integration tests once the signer is ready.

Follow-ups will replace the stub with the real verifier (key-based offline verification) and integrate `verify-bundle` into `install` to run automatically before unpack.

## UX / Output
- On success, prints a concise summary (bundle id/version, manifest hash, files verified count).
- On failure, prints the first failing artifact path + expected vs actual digest and returns exit code `2`.
- On signature verifier unimplemented, prints: "signature verification is not available in this installer build" and returns exit code `2`.

## Testing
- `go test ./...`
- Added unit tests in `cmd/verify_bundle_test.go` and `internal/verify/verify_test.go`

## Notes / Constraints
- No network calls; everything operates on local filesystem paths.
- Fail-closed by design: missing file or mismatched digest => hard failure.
- No break-glass/override flags yet; those will be added as a separate PR with security review (to keep the initial command behavior strict).

## Screenshots / Example
`$ redwood-private-installer verify-bundle --bundle ./redwood-private-offline-bundle.tgz`
- For now, this will fail at signature verification until the signer integration lands (expected in subsequent PRs).
commits: cmd: add verify-bundle subcommand + help text
verify: add manifest loader + sha256 digest verification
verify: introduce SignatureVerifier interface + stub implementation
tests: add unit coverage for verify-bundle error handling and exit codes
chore: gofmt + small refactors for readability
review_conversation:
Marcus Lin: Returning success when signature verification is stubbed would be a footgun. Can we ensure this returns non-zero until real verification is implemented?
Ethan Park: Yep. Current behavior returns exit code 2 with ErrSignatureVerificationUnimplemented and prints an explicit message. Added a unit test for it as well.

Connor O'Brien: +1 on landing the command early. Can we keep exit codes stable? Release automation will depend on this.
Ethan Park: Added `internal/errors/exit_codes.go` and tests asserting the mapping. We can treat these as public contract.

Benji Okafor: Minor: naming. `verify-bundle` vs `verify offline-bundle`? Also, can the command accept both a directory and a tarball path?
Ethan Park: Kept it as `verify-bundle` to avoid future renames. This PR supports directory bundles only; tarball support will land with unpack/install integration so we can avoid double-extracting. Left a TODO in `cmd/verify_bundle.go`.

Kevin Osei: For auditability, please ensure the error output includes which file failed digest verification and expected/actual.
Ethan Park: Added to the failure message and included in tests (`TestVerifyBundle_DigestMismatch_PrintsExpectedActual`).
release_notes: Private installer now includes a `verify-bundle` CLI command for offline bundle manifest/digest checks, with signature verification wiring (stubbed until signer integration lands).
